arguments.summary:
Security assessment of the AIT-GUI repository (NASA AMMOS). The codebase is a Python/JS web application (Bottle framework) providing telemetry and command interfaces for AIT (Autonomous Integrative Technologies). The threat model identifies many HTTP routes that accept untrusted input, several of which lead to privileged operations (command execution, script running, sequence management). Key findings centre on insufficient input validation and missing authorisation/authentication checks at critical sinks, creating potential command injection and privilege escalation risks.

The repository contains 97 files, primarily Python (ait/gui/__init__.py) and JavaScript static assets. Entry points are numerous HTTP POST/GET routes defined via @App.route decorators, many handling commands, scripts, sequences, and telemetry. Trust boundaries are enforced via TLS, rate limiting, and a cross‑origin resource sharing (CORS) origin check in middleware, but not all routes inherit that check.

The investigation identified a command‑injection vector in the /cmd handler where the raw form parameter "command" is split and passed to self.send(). No sanitisation or allow‑list validation is performed, and the method does not re‑apply the origin‑based CORS guard present elsewhere. Additional routes (e.g., /script/run, /script/*) likely have similar patterns but were not fully traced due to scope limits.

Findings are grounded in source excerpts from ait/gui/__init__.py (lines 444‑463 for handle_cmd, lines 1220‑1278 for script run handlers) and the threat‑model entry‑point list.

findings.title: Command Injection via /cmd endpoint
findings.missing_control: Input validation / allow‑list; output encoding; origin CORS check
findings.attacker_prerequisites: Ability to send a POST request with a form field named 'command' to the AIT-GUI server; no authentication required on this route.
findings.impact: An attacker could inject arbitrary shell commands that the server's send() method executes, potentially leading to full compromise of the host environment.
findings.counterevidence: The send() method is inherited from the Plugin base class; its implementation was not fully inspected, but the pass‑through of unsanitised user data is a classic injection pattern.
unresolved_assumptions: Exact behaviour of self.send() (whether it shells out)

findings.title: Missing authentication on many privileged routes
findings.entry_point: GET /cmd (and numerous other routes listed in threat model)
findings.vulnerable_operation: Route handlers accept requests without verifying user identity or session permissions
findings.attacker_prerequisites: Network access to the AIT-GUI instance; no additional prerequisites beyond reaching the endpoint.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated actors can invoke command, script, and sequence operations, bypassing intended access controls.
findings.counterevidence: The threat model lists auth_required: false for the majority of routes, indicating intentional open‑access design; however, this may be a misconfiguration for a production system.
unresolved_assumptions: Whether intended deployment relies on reverse‑proxy authentication

findings.title: Cross‑Site Request Forgery (CSRF) risk on state‑changing routes
findings.vulnerable_operation: Lack of CSRF tokens on POST endpoints that modify state
findings.attacker_prerequisites: A malicious web page can craft a form that submits to /cmd when a logged‑in operator visits it.
findings.impact: If an authenticated operator is tricked into loading a malicious page, arbitrary commands may be executed on their behalf.
findings.counterevidence: Same‑origin policy and Referer‑based checks exist for some routes, but not all, and they do not constitute full CSRF mitigation.
unresolved_assumptions: Whether the application expects browser‑based operators only

findings.title: Potential command injection in script‑run handlers
findings.vulnerable_operation: User‑provided script content passed to execution path without sanitisation
findings.missing_control: Input validation, sandboxing, or allow‑list of permitted scripts
findings.attacker_prerequisites: Ability to POST to /script/run; no auth required.
findings.impact: Remote code execution via script execution.
findings.counterevidence: Not fully inspected; similar pattern to /cmd handler.
unresolved_assumptions: Exact execution mechanism of script runner
